course_title: Jr/Sr Coll: LatAm&NonWest Wrld: Partition of India, 1947
subject: HIST
course_description: All history majors except those who complete the Honors Program must take two colloquia ( HIST 487 , 488 or 489 ). Each colloquium treats a special theme by reading, discussion, and writing of papers. Enrollment in each is limited to twelve; non-majors are welcome within space limitations.
course_notes: This seminar deals with the memory/history of the Partition of British India in 1947, an event that resulted in the establishment of the nation-states of India, Pakistan and (in time) Bangladesh. It investigates official and unofficial histories of this turning point, when 2 - 3 million people died and over 10 million became refugees, and juxtaposes them with the memories of survivors. We investigate the recasting of the past and the present in the new nation-states by examining (1) official and academic histories, the media, fiction and films; (2) oral accounts reflecting the new identities and perspectives of local groups, communities and regions, divided as these are by gender, caste and class. Close reading, reflection and discussion of a range of written and visual sources helps students from diverse disciplinary backgrounds develop a critical approach to the understanding of modern societies and their contested histories. Students will analyze the writings of historians such as Ayesha Jalal, Gyan Pandey and Vazira Zamindar; oral histories by Urvashi Butalia, Kamla Bhasin, Ritu Menon and others; contemporary fiction of Manto, Rajinder Singh Bedi, and others; and films such as Deepa Mehta's `Earth, M. S. Sathyu's `Garam Hawa,' and Richard Attenborough's `Gandhi.'
